# 07-legacy-cookie-cutover: Apply the minimal legacy LocalUser cookie change

Change only the LocalUser Katana cookie registration and supporting legacy configuration. Explicitly set `.AspNet.LocalUser` and the proven interoperability values, construct the shared Data Protection provider from settings resolved through the existing `web.config` wrapper and credential factories, and resolve the keyed `ICoreFileStorageService`/official Key Vault integration as singletons. The format switch occurs at the slot swap, with one-time session loss at swap or rollback accepted.

Keep the legacy host as the sole issuer and refresher during this phase: disable competing ASP.NET Core sliding renewal and do not call `SignInAsync` for proxied requests. Preserve login paths, secure-cookie behavior, six-hour expiry, sliding expiration, claims, external-login flow, temporary external cookie, admin bearer authentication, anti-forgery protection, machine-key consumers, controllers, views, EF6, SQL, storage selection, and the rest of the OWIN pipeline.

**Done when**: Targeted legacy authentication tests and the task `03` compatibility suite pass against production-equivalent registration, a proxied authenticated request receives at most the legacy host's single renewal, invalid cookies still permit anonymous proxy fallback, and the legacy application remains independently deployable.

## Repository research (2026-09-08)

- The retained Katana registration is isolated to `LocalUserAuthenticator`. It already preserves active `LocalUser` authentication, HTTP-only and `RequireSSL`-driven secure behavior, `/users/account/LogOn`, six-hour expiry, sliding renewal, and the default sign-in type. The cutover only needs to make the existing `.AspNet.LocalUser` name and `/` path explicit, replace `TicketDataFormat` with `AspNetTicketDataFormat`/`DataProtectorShim`, and use the Core-compatible `Microsoft.Owin.Security.Interop.ChunkingCookieManager`.
- Task `03` established the exact wire contract in `SharedCookieConstants`: `.AspNet.LocalUser`, scheme `LocalUser`, application discriminator `NuGetGallery`, and purpose chain `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.Cookies.CookieAuthenticationMiddleware` / `LocalUser` / `v2`. Its executable harness already proves claim, expiry, tampering, wrong-key/purpose, old-machine-key, and `chunks-N` compatibility in both directions.
- Task `04` added the production storage and encryption foundations. `StorageDependent` already registers the Data Protection `FileStorageXmlRepository` as a singleton and groups its keyed `ICoreFileStorageService` by the injected `Gallery.AzureStorage.DataProtection.ConnectionString`; filesystem registration resolves the same repository over the existing singleton filesystem storage.
- `ConfigurationService.Initialize()` is the existing `web.config` wrapper and `$$secret$$` injection boundary. `IAppConfiguration.ToSharedDataProtectionConfiguration()` normalizes its injected storage/settings values. `SecretReaderFactory` already creates the canonical `KeyVaultConfiguration` through managed-identity or certificate settings, and `KeyVaultKeyEncryptionKeyResolver` uses the official Azure `IKeyEncryptionKeyResolver` abstraction and repository credential factory.
- The legacy Autofac container imports an `IServiceCollection`, so the shared Data Protection builder can be registered in the existing root container and consume the singleton repository and resolver rather than building a second container. Production is identified by the established `Gallery.Environment == "Prod"` value; production validation therefore remains fail-closed while local filesystem development remains independently runnable without Azure.
- The ASP.NET Core host already uses the same constants and shared repository, has `SlidingExpiration = false`, and contains no `SignInAsync` call. Its authentication/authorization middleware runs before the terminal YARP route, allowing invalid cookies to remain anonymous while forwarding them to the legacy authority; YARP passes the legacy response's single `Set-Cookie` renewal through unchanged.
- `migrating-owin-cookie-auth` does not apply: Katana remains supported and is intentionally retained as the sole issuer/refresher. External temporary cookies, admin bearer middleware, antiforgery/machine-key configuration, controllers, views, EF6, SQL, other storage registrations, and all other OWIN middleware remain untouched.

## Planned affected files

- `src/NuGetGallery.Services/Authentication/Providers/LocalUser/LocalUserAuthenticator.cs` and its project reference — apply only the explicit shared-cookie wire format.
- `src/NuGetGallery.Services/Configuration/ConfigurationService.cs` and `SecretReaderFactory.cs` — retain and expose the one canonical Key Vault configuration created by existing wrapper/credential logic.
- `src/NuGetGallery/App_Start/DefaultDependenciesModule.cs` — register the normalized configuration, official Key Vault resolver, and shared Data Protection provider as singletons over the existing keyed repository/storage.
- Focused legacy and proxy tests plus the task `03` harness — verify production-equivalent registration, one legacy renewal, anonymous invalid-cookie fallback, and standalone legacy startup.
